problem: Django REST Framework endpoint loading Articles with nested Tags triggers N+1. Added prefetch_related('tags') but nested Tag.category still causes separate queries per tag.
solution: Dead ends: simple prefetch_related only handles one level. Using depth= on serializer makes it worse. Unlock: Use Prefetch() object with custom queryset — prefetch_related(Prefetch('tags', queryset=Tag.objects.select_related('category'))). This chains eager loading at each level. Result: 3 queries total regardless of result count.

problem: React ThemeContext causes full tree re-render on every theme token change (colors, spacing) even though most components only use 1-2 tokens. useMemo on value object doesn't help.
solution: Dead ends: useMemo on the context value doesn't help because child components still consume the whole object. React.memo on children doesn't help because context bypasses memo. Unlock: Split into multiple focused contexts (ThemeColorContext, ThemeSpacingContext) so components only subscribe to what they use. Or use a selector pattern with use-context-selector library. Or migrate to zustand/jotai which have built-in selectors.

problem: Node.js Transform stream: async database lookups per record cause output to arrive in random order instead of preserving CSV row order.
solution: Dead ends: objectMode doesn't help with ordering. Increasing highWaterMark makes it worse. Piping through a sort step loses streaming benefits. Unlock: Assign sequence numbers before processing. Buffer output: hold results until the next expected sequence number is ready. Emit in order. Or use p-transform with concurrency + ordered option. Or collect all, Promise.all, then write sequentially if dataset fits in memory.

problem: Prisma interactive transaction ($transaction) randomly fails with P2034 when two API requests update same user record simultaneously. Retrying causes double-charge.
solution: Dead ends: retrying the entire transaction causes duplicate side effects. Increasing transaction timeout just delays the error. Using serializable isolation alone doesn't prevent the double-charge. Unlock: Optimistic locking with version field. Add version: Int to the model. UPDATE WHERE version = expected_version. If 0 rows affected, return 409 Conflict. The caller retries with fresh data. This is atomic and prevents both lost updates and double processing.

problem: Next.js 14 App Router: Map object from Server Component to Client Component fails serialization. JSON.stringify loses Map methods.
solution: Dead ends: JSON.stringify converts Map to {}. Using Array.from(map) loses the Map type on client. Wrapping in useMemo doesn't help with SSR. Unlock: Serialize to plain object: Object.fromEntries(map) on server, reconstruct with new Map(Object.entries(obj)) on client. For complex types, use superjson which handles Maps, Sets, Dates natively. Pass as JSON string and parse on client.

problem: FastAPI async endpoint hangs when calling a sync library function that internally uses asyncio.run(). The sync library was designed for non-async callers.
solution: Dead ends: await doesn't work on sync functions. asyncio.run() inside async context raises 'event loop already running'. nest_asyncio is a hack that can cause subtle bugs. Unlock: Use loop.run_in_executor(None, sync_function) to run in a thread pool — the sync function gets its own event loop in the thread. Or asyncio.to_thread(sync_function) in Python 3.9+. This isolates the nested event loop in a separate thread.

problem: TypeScript utility type to extract optional keys: type OptionalKeys<T> = keyof T doesn't distinguish optional from required. Using undefined extends T[K] matches both 'name?: string' and 'name: string | undefined'.
solution: Dead ends: undefined extends T[K] can't distinguish optional from explicitly-undefined. Checking for Partial<T> doesn't help because it makes everything optional. Unlock: Use {} extends Pick<T, K> — this is true ONLY for optional keys because {} satisfies an object type with only optional properties. Full type: type OptionalKeys<T> = { [K in keyof T]-?: {} extends Pick<T, K> ? K : never }[keyof T]. The -? removes optional modifier during the mapped type check.

problem: Java Spring Boot app OOMKilled in Kubernetes despite -Xmx2g and container limit 3Gi. JVM uses 2.8Gi total.
solution: Dead ends: increasing container limit is not sustainable. -Xmx only controls heap. Thread dump doesn't show heap issues. Unlock: JVM uses memory beyond heap: Metaspace (~200MB), thread stacks (1MB × thread_count), direct byte buffers, GC overhead (~10-15% of heap), JIT code cache (~240MB). Use -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 instead of fixed -Xmx. Enable -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary to audit. Formula: container_limit >= heap + metaspace + (threads × 1MB) + GC_overhead + direct_buffers + 256MB_safety.

problem: Apollo GraphQL DataLoader caches results across HTTP requests — first request's data leaks to subsequent requests from different users.
solution: Dead ends: adding cache: false to queries doesn't affect DataLoader. Clearing Apollo Client cache doesn't clear DataLoader cache. Using maxBatchSize=1 defeats the purpose. Unlock: DataLoader must be per-request, not per-server. Create new instances in the GraphQL context: context: ({ req }) => ({ loaders: createLoaders(req.user) }). Each request gets fresh loader with empty cache. Never share DataLoader instances across requests.

problem: Rust: need to share config struct across multiple tokio::spawn tasks. Moving it into one closure makes it unavailable for others.
solution: Dead ends: borrowing doesn't work because spawned tasks require 'static lifetime. Cloning the whole config wastes memory. Using global static requires unsafe. Unlock: Wrap in Arc: let config = Arc::new(config); For each task: let cfg = Arc::clone(&config); tokio::spawn(async move { use cfg }). Arc is cheap (reference counting). For mutation, use Arc<RwLock<Config>> — readers don't block each other. Prefer RwLock over Mutex for read-heavy configs.

problem: Webpack 5 dynamic import() creates circular chunk dependency between two route bundles that both import from a shared index.ts barrel file.
solution: Dead ends: optimization.splitChunks extracts shared code but doesn't break the barrel-induced cycle. Moving the shared code to a separate chunk still has circular references through the barrel re-exports. Unlock: Replace barrel file imports with direct module imports. Change import { X } from './features' to import { X } from './features/auth/utils'. Set sideEffects: false in package.json so webpack can tree-shake. Verify with webpack-bundle-analyzer that chunks are acyclic.

problem: PostgreSQL query on 50M row orders table: WHERE status='pending' AND date > NOW()-24h. Index exists on (status, date) but planner uses seqscan. EXPLAIN shows rows estimate is way off.
solution: Dead ends: Full composite index on (status, date) includes all 50M rows — too large for cache. ANALYZE doesn't help because the combined selectivity estimate is wrong. Force index scan with SET enable_seqscan=off is a bandaid. Unlock: CREATE INDEX idx_pending ON orders(date) WHERE status='pending' — partial index. Only indexes the ~50K pending rows. It's tiny, always in memory, and the planner loves it. Also run ANALYZE to update statistics for the partial index.

problem: Docker build takes 8 min because npm install reruns on every source code change. The COPY . . step before RUN npm install invalidates the cache.
solution: Dead ends: using --mount=type=cache helps but doesn't fully solve. Multi-stage build still runs npm install if any file changed. Unlock: Copy package files FIRST: COPY package*.json ./ → RUN npm ci --only=production → COPY . . Docker caches each layer. If only source changed (not package.json), npm ci layer stays cached. Add .dockerignore with node_modules to prevent COPY conflicts. Use multi-stage for build vs runtime separation.

problem: Celery tasks silently disappear after Redis broker restart. Using acks_late=True but tasks running >1h get redelivered to another worker (duplicate processing).
solution: Dead ends: acks_late alone causes redelivery when visibility_timeout expires. Increasing visibility_timeout to 24h means crashed tasks aren't retried for a day. Using acks_on_failure_or_timeout doesn't prevent redelivery during normal execution. Unlock: (1) Set visibility_timeout > max_task_duration + margin. (2) Make tasks idempotent with unique execution ID. (3) Add task_reject_on_worker_lost=True so tasks are requeued on crash, not lost. (4) For very long tasks, periodically extend the visibility timeout with a heartbeat.

problem: React Suspense: three child components each fetch data independently with useSuspenseQuery. Components load sequentially (waterfall) — each waits for the previous to resolve.
solution: Dead ends: Wrapping all in one Suspense boundary makes them sequential because React suspends at the first throw. Separate Suspense boundaries show 3 loading states (bad UX). useQueries doesn't work with Suspense. Unlock: Start all fetches BEFORE render (render-as-you-fetch). In route loader or parent component: const p1 = fetchA(); const p2 = fetchB(); Pass promises down. Children use() the promises. All fetches run in parallel because they started before any component suspended.

problem: Python plugin system with __init_subclass__ doesn't auto-discover plugin classes in subdirectories of the plugins package.
solution: Dead ends: __init_subclass__ only fires when the module is imported. Python doesn't auto-import submodules. Using __init__.py with wildcard imports is brittle and manual. Unlock: At app startup, recursively import all submodules: import pkgutil, importlib; for importer, modname, ispkg in pkgutil.walk_packages(plugins.__path__, plugins.__name__ + '.'): importlib.import_module(modname). This triggers __init_subclass__ on every plugin class. Alternative: use setuptools entry_points for decoupled discovery.

problem: Go HTTP middleware: recover() in middleware doesn't catch panics from goroutines spawned in handlers.
solution: Dead ends: defer recover() only catches panics in the current goroutine. Wrapping the handler in recover() has no effect on child goroutines. Setting GOTRACEBACK doesn't help. Unlock: Each goroutine needs its own defer recover(). Wrap all spawned goroutines: go func() { defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { log.Error('panic in goroutine', r) } }(); doWork() }(). Better: use errgroup.Group which coordinates multiple goroutines and surfaces panics. Create a safeGo() helper to enforce this pattern.

problem: CSS Grid: child with position:absolute makes parent grid row collapse to 0 height because absolutely positioned elements leave normal flow.
solution: Dead ends: setting explicit height on grid row defeats the auto-sizing purpose. Using min-height: 100% on absolute child creates circular dependency. Flexbox fallback loses grid alignment benefits. Unlock: Use CSS Grid's native element overlap instead of position:absolute. Place both elements in same grid cell: grid-row: 1; grid-column: 1 on both elements. Use z-index to control stacking. The grid cell auto-sizes to fit both elements' content. This is the grid-native way to overlap without breaking flow.

problem: JWT verification accepts forged tokens: attacker uses RS256 public key as HS256 secret (algorithm confusion attack).
solution: Dead ends: checking token signature passes because the verification uses the public key material for HMAC. Rotating keys doesn't help if algorithm isn't pinned. Adding token expiry doesn't prevent forged tokens within the window. Unlock: ALWAYS specify the expected algorithm in verify(): jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] }). Never let the token's 'alg' header choose the verification method. This is CVE-2016-5431. Server MUST pin the algorithm. Also validate issuer and audience claims.

problem: Redis memory doubles overnight despite TTL on all keys. INFO shows 8GB used but only 200K keys. Output buffers for slow pub/sub subscribers consuming memory.
solution: Dead ends: reducing TTL doesn't help — the memory is in client output buffers, not key storage. maxmemory-policy evicts keys but not buffers. Monitoring key sizes shows nothing unusual. Unlock: Set client-output-buffer-limit pubsub 32mb 8mb 60 (hard 32MB, soft 8MB for 60s). Monitor with CLIENT LIST for slow subscribers. Disconnect clients that can't keep up. For durable messaging, migrate from Pub/Sub to Redis Streams with consumer groups — Streams handle backpressure and persistence natively.
